title: 土質力学Ⅱ
subtitle: Soil Mechanics II
educationalGoal:
This course aims to provide a basic knowledge of percolation of soil and concept of effective stress. As appicable examples fo soil water drainage, stability of dam or sheet pile coffer dam by using flow net will be learned.
Secondary, the differences between total and effective stress in Mohr's circle should be understand and be able to choose proper parameters of strength, internal friction and adhesive stress.
advice:
This course will impart a solid grounding in Soil Mechanics. The contents are shown as followings.
1. Soil compaction
Compacting factor test, characteristics of compacted soil.

2.Percolation of soil
Darcy's law, permeability, flownet, boiling and piping, drainage

3.Shear strength of soil
Shear strength, Mohr's circle, testing method of shear stregth, shear properties of sand and clay, increasing strength by consolidation
requiredKnowledge:
Knowledge of basis of Mechanics and enough knowledge of Soil Mechanics I.
Reading textbook in advance is available to easy understanding.

activityGoals.body: be able to understand concept of water head / potential and hydraulic gradient. [0.2K]
be able to estimate flux and stability of boiling by using flow net. [0.2K]
be able to understand Mohr and Coulomb criterion and specify parameters by laboratory test results. [0.2K]
be able to understand the differences between total and efferctive stress. [0.2K]
be able to understand characteristics of soil compaction. [0.2K]

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Fully understand the behavioral goals of Soil Mechanics II, and acquire basic skills as an engineer.
(2) Choose aproprieate laboratory tests against design condition and specify proper soil parameters.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Understand the behavioral goals of Soil Mechanics II, the basic properies of soil by from physical soil tests as an engineer.
(2) Calculate stability of boiling and obtain soil compaction factor.
